column1: # SPLIT-RECONSTRUCTION ratio sweep + scale-matched constants + the 0.01x latent arms.
# User direction 2026-09-20. PHASE 1: SINGLE-CELL targets (target_pb_k=1, the default).
# Phase 2 (group-mean targets) is deliberately held back so denoising and weighting are not
# confounded.
# WHY. F-recon1: smooth_l1(pred, target) is ~99.8% CONTROL RECONSTRUCTION on M03
# (||D(z_ctrl)-c|| = 15.34 vs a true effect size of 2.88), so the perturbation is supervised by
# ~0.2% of that term's gradient. Splitting it lets the two be weighted independently:
#     L_ctrl  = recon(D(z_ctrl), ctrl)                 pass the control through
#     L_delta = recon(pred - D(z_ctrl), target - ctrl) predict the CHANGE
# ⚠️ WHY A RATIO SWEEP AND NOT SCALE-MATCHED CONSTANTS. Measured on the real training path,
# UNWEIGHTED, the two terms do NOT hold a fixed ratio -- it moves 8x in three epochs:
# L_ctrl decays as the autoencoder learns the passthrough; L_delta is flat. Every other
# scale-matched weight in this campaign (nb_scale, dcos 0.01, delta_mag 0.01363, the latent
# parity weights) was a CONSTANT from a one-off measurement, which was sound because those
# ratios were stable. Here a weight balancing the terms at epoch 1 leaves the delta 8x
# over-weighted by epoch 3. So the axis swept is the RATIO, anchored at 1:1.
# S-ARMS ARE THE SCALE-MATCHED CONTROL, and they are NOT in the (1, k) ratio family. They set
# both weights so the two terms contribute EQUALLY at the measured converged point while
# holding the TOTAL reconstruction contribution unchanged -- i.e. each gets half of
# The ratio arms keep w_ctrl = 1, so their TOTAL recon grows with w_delta and its balance
# against dcos shifts; the S-arms hold that balance fixed. That is the difference being tested.
# ⚠️ 0.813/1.298 come from the rhj_smoke config (720 cells/epoch, 3 epochs). The TREND
# transfers; the endpoint does not. Read each arm's printed [recon-split] trajectory.
# T-ARMS: P11 (latent both at 0.1x parity) was the best combination arm on M03 -- closest
# pearson_delta (-0.0009), best mae (0.0211) and the best overlap_at_N in that table (0.0738 vs
# M03's 0.0722). This takes the same shape an order of magnitude lower, 0.01x parity, on both
# bases. M03 parity: lmse 0.0157, lcos 0.0097. M06 parity: lmse 0.0044, lcos 0.0059.
# BASES, held fixed: M03 = dcos 0.01, mag 0. M06 = dcos 0.5, mag 0.01363. Everything else is arm
# s313 (adjacency_map, batch 2048, lr 1e-3, decoder_lr 1e-3, cosine_loss_weight 0.5, film
# multiplicative_only, fh 256, mean-free, 30 epochs, seed 42).
# READ AGAINST (test, uncalibrated, 5/5): M03 0.3679/0.0212/0.0722/0.6715 ·
# M06 0.3681/0.0232/0.0703/0.7047. `mae` is an ERROR: LOWER IS BETTER.
# ANCHORS: meanpert 0.1324 · transfer 0.2323 · experimental 0.3722 (mae 0.0257).
# PRE-REGISTERED. mae falls below M03's 0.0212 while pearson_delta holds -> F-recon1's
# hypothesis is right: mae was immovable because every prior lever acted on the perturbation
# while mae is dominated by control reconstruction. mae flat across all ratios -> the hypothesis
# is wrong and mae is limited by something else entirely. S-arm != its neighbouring ratio arms
# -> the recon-vs-dcos total balance matters independently of the internal split.
